We use the quotient rule with the numerator $u(x)=\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}$ and the denominator $v(x)=2x.$ 

Differentiating $u(x)$ and $v(x),$ we have

$$
{u}^{′}(x)=\frac{1}{2x\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}},\,{v}^{′}(x)=2.
$$

Note that we used the chain rule to differentiate $u.$

Now, applying the quotient rule and simplifying, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{1}{2x\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}})(2x)-(\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡x})(2)}{(2x)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}}-2\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}}{4{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1-2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{4{x}^{2}\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
